reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports Al–Al clustering and a compression-induced clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, but provides no data on tensile loading as a baseline, nor on the claimed property improvements (strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, cryogenic toughness). Thus, two key premises are unsupported.
premises: Al–Al clustering dominates in low-Al Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs
High-temperature compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition
This transition is specific to compressive (vs. tensile) loading
The ordering transition improves high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness
